label: baseline (unmodified system, commit 7af8800)
captured_from: real frontend at http://127.0.0.1:5173 -> LinkedIn Writer -> Generate

brief.topic: How I built a fully local AI agent that runs on a CPU-only laptop: a routing harness that sends every task to the cheapest processor that can answer it reliably, so the language model is the last resort instead of the default.
brief.audience: AI engineering hiring managers and companies that want AI automation built
brief.facts: Measured on one benchmark run of 23 tasks, LLM-only baseline vs the routing harness on the same machine: LLM calls 23 to 4 (-82.6%). Tokens 8364 to 2214 (-73.5%). Total latency 283.8s to 48.4s (-83.0%). CPU time 2575.5s to 477.8s (-81.5%). Accuracy 39.1% to 100%. 19 of the 23 tasks were answered with no LLM call at all. Fully offline, CPU only: 18 logical cores, 16.7 GB RAM, no GPU. Model is Qwen1.5-1.8B-chat Q4_K_M via llama.cpp. Layers in order: deterministic tools, NLP, classical ML, RAG retrieval, then the LLM last.

processor_path: linkedin_writer.select_examples (collapse to documents, cap 700 chars, k=2)
note_on_routing: The Writer page calls /api/writer/generate, which invokes the linkedin_writer service directly. The router chain creative_generation -> [p_linkedin_writer] wraps the same service for Chat/Tasks. No router misrouting is involved in this run.

prompt.system: You are a LinkedIn ghostwriter that reproduces one specific author's voice. Write only the post text - no preamble, no explanation, no markdown headers, no quotation marks around the post. Never invent metrics, dates, company names or achievements that are not in the provided context.
prompt.reconstruction_note: Rebuilt offline from the same inputs and example doc_ids; char count matched the API-reported 3311 exactly, so the prompt below is byte-identical to what the model received.
prompt.facts_block_header: FACTS YOU MAY USE (do not add others):
constraints_emitted: Use about 2 short paragraphs, one or two sentences each.
Average sentence length around 19 words; never exceed 40.
Open with a direct factual statement about the topic.
Write plainly and concretely, the way an engineer describes what they built.
Do not use bullet points unless the topic is a list.
End with at most 5 hashtags on their own line.
No generic LinkedIn filler and no hype words.
Do not copy any sentence from the examples verbatim.
Use only the facts given above; if a number is not provided, do not state one.
Audience: AI engineering hiring managers and companies that want AI automation built.
End with a call to action of type: hiring.

output:
I built a routing harness that sends every task to the cheapest processor that can answer it reliably, making the language model the last resort. This setup reduces LLM calls and latency, optimizing performance on a CPU-only laptop. 🛠️

Try it out and see the difference in efficiency and accuracy. Hiring for more engineers with a practical approach to AI.
